newsitem.title: GERMANY: German four-month net new borrowing up 73 pct - Buba.
newsitem.headline: German four-month net new borrowing up 73 pct - Buba.

text.p: Germany's federal, regional and municipal authorities borrowed a net 48.9 billion marks ($28.2 billion) in the first four months of 1997, a rise of 73 percent or 20.6 billion marks from the 1996 period, the Bundesbank said on Wednesday.
A net 40 billion marks came from selling securities.
Another 7.5 billion marks came from long-term direct loans and two billion marks came from money market loans and short-term bank loans, the German central bank said in its June monthly report.
The federal government was the main borrower, taking up a net 38 billion marks in new debt, with 26.5 billion marks coming from bond issues, the central bank said.
